headline: Stocks bounce on Oracle's AI blowout despite hawkish CPI surprise
body: Major indices snapped a four-session losing streak Friday, with the Dow climbing 0.98% to 52,573.29, the S&P 500 up 0.86% to 7,656.98, and the Nasdaq gaining 0.96% to 26,333.04. The rally came even as the August CPI report ran hotter than hoped — headline inflation up 0.4% for the month and 3.4% year-over-year, core CPI up 0.3% — pushing futures-implied odds of a rate hike at next week's September 16-17 Fed meeting to roughly 85%, up sharply from about 70% a day earlier. Easing crude prices, with WTI down 2.4% to just above $100 and Brent off nearly 3%, offset some of the rate anxiety. The net effect was a market willing to look past a more hawkish repricing when a strong single-stock catalyst was in play, at least for one session.

That catalyst was Oracle, whose shares jumped as much as 7% in premarket trading after a blowout quarter — cloud infrastructure revenue up 121%, an AI contract backlog swelling to roughly $664 billion, and management noting that demand for AI training and inference capacity is outpacing supply. The move underscores how concentrated conviction remains in AI-infrastructure names even as the broader rate backdrop turns less friendly. Retail-sentiment channels read more mixed: trading forums carried an anxious, loss-focused tone this week, including viral posts about outsized margin calls, while trending-ticker activity skewed toward speculative small- and mid-cap names and split opinion on at least one major AI-adjacent chip stock's valuation. On balance, today's read leans more on a single earnings catalyst and shifting rate odds than on any unified social-sentiment wave.
